places.name: Bình Thủy Môn
places.size: An old minor-sect seat, now the Strangers' Hall after the sect moved away in 1116: about 40 buildings stepping up a grassy headland about 300 m across, with a quay and a ferry landing. Once 60 ferrymen and sailors; now a hostel and shrine run by a few caretakers, still bustling with ferry passengers.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), a low green headland at sea level over the strait, grassland, coast. Vassal of Lạc Hà Tông. The seat moved to the crab flats Cự Ngao Chử (place 302) in 1116; this place stays as the Strangers' Hall. Nearest: spring Tha Hương Tuyền (90 km), village Lãng Thạch Thôn (158 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Dusk. The green lanterns on the mast are being lit one by one, a ferry noses out into the strait, and in the halls travellers sleep who have each written a home village on a lantern.
places.subject: The place: Bình Thủy Môn, the Strangers' Hall, a former sect seat on a low green headland above a strait. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a broad rolling green grassy peninsula juts into the sea on the right, a river inland and a small rocky point at its lower tip. Rolling green grass covers the headland to its tip, with the far shore of the strait a low blue line. The settlement: about forty buildings with grey-tile roofs and pale walls stepping up the slope in five tiers to one high hall, the tallest outline on the headland: below it two long hostels, a hall of benches where ferry passengers wait, a small shipwright's yard with a hull on stocks, a ferry office with a long timber landing, a shrine court, and a few dozen households of caretakers and boatmen; a stone stair leads down to a small quay where five ferries, broad and flat, are tied. Signature element: on the very tip of the headland a tall slender mast, far taller than any roof, hung with hundreds of tiny green lanterns in rising rows, each a home village's name, lit at dusk so that the mast glows green like a lit tree; a few ferries crossing the strait carry green lights. Life at scale: a modest, busy crossing place full of tiny travellers with bundles queuing at the landing, a crowd of perhaps two hundred figures, none of whom live here. Light: deep gold dusk light from the upper left, the turquoise water darkening, green lantern points glowing, long shadows.

places.name: Đàm Ảnh Thành
places.size: A port city of about 35,000 people: walls about 2 km long, some 8,000 grey roofs in seven districts around a great round pool about 400 m across, a river quay with about 60 boats.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), flat grassland shore at sea level where a river meets the sea, a port. Held by Lạc Hà Tông; built by the sailors' sect Cô Phàm Các in 410. Nearest: spirit vein Tinh Di Mạch (175 km), village Tình Sa Thôn (214 km), the ruin Bích Không Cảng (255 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A still noon with big white clouds: the pool is a perfect mirror and the city lies upside down in it, painters at their easels around the rim.
places.subject: The place: Đàm Ảnh Thành, the City of the Pool's Reflections, a walled port city on an island's grassy shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at noon on a clear day with large soft white clouds; green rolling hills and farmland with a few dark groves, two rivers winding down from the west and meeting at the head of a narrow blue sea inlet that opens to the north-east. The city: low rectangular grey stone walls with square gate towers and a river gate, enclosing about eight thousand grey-tile roofs in seven districts: a fishers' quarter with net yards, a trade district of warehouses and counting houses along the river quay where about sixty boats are tied, a painters' quarter with open studios and roofs of pale canvas awnings, wide merchants' houses, the grey halls of the ruling sect with a garden court, and long ranks of homes. Signature element: in the heart of the city lies a huge perfectly round pool, about four hundred paces across, mirror-still, so that the clouds and the city's own roofs lie upside down in it with perfect clarity; ringed with about thirty small open pavilions with upturned grey roofs, and on their stone terraces many tiny painters at easels, some working on canvases held up to the sky; a blind old man sits alone on the rim. A circular promenade of pale stone circles the pool. Life at scale: tens of thousands of residents, carts on the main streets, sails on the river. Light: bright clean noon light from the upper left, soft shadows, the pool's mirror image a blue-and-white second sky.

places.name: Tương Phùng Thị
places.size: A floating market of about 600 boats lashed into a raft about 400 m by 150 m, with some 3,000 traders and visitors on any day; the shape changes daily. A little shore of about 30 sheds at the quay.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland coast at sea level, a port at the quay below Bình Thủy Môn. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Founded 525. The strait ferries leave from its outer boats. Nearest: spirit vein Bình Tung Mạch (100 km), ruin Phiêu Bồng Quán (103 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A bright, breezy morning: boats are drifting in and out of the raft and the green awnings flutter like duckweed on the strait.
places.subject: The place: Tương Phùng Thị, the Market of Chance Meetings, a market built half on the water. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright breezy morning; a rounded grassy cape of green and tawny hills with scattered dark groves and a stream at the lower left, the sea on all other sides. Beyond the cape the strait water is turquoise and dotted with a few free sails. The market: about six hundred boats of every size, from rowing skiffs to broad flat barges, lashed side by side into an irregular floating raft that sprawls out from the quay in lobes and peninsulas, about four hundred paces long, with narrow lanes of open water between its parts; planks and rope bridges link the boats; on every boat a stall: awnings of faded green, bolts of cloth, baskets of fish, jars of oil, bright fruit, trinkets, rolls of rope, caged birds. Some boats are drifting free at the edge, a few new ones coming in with poles, a few leaving; no stall appears where the next would expect it. Signature element: the green awnings, hundreds, faded to many shades of green, drifting and nodding with the water like duckweed spread across the strait. At the raft's outer edge, five large ferry-barges with high bow-ramps are loading passengers. Thousands of tiny figures walk the planks, meet, embrace, wave. Life at scale: a living, shifting crowd, a spectacle of chance. Light: bright morning sun from the upper left, glittering ripples, small crisp shadows under each awning.

places.name: Xích Ngạn Trấn
places.size: A small walled cliff-top town of about 6,000 people: about 1,400 grey roofs inside a wall about 700 m by 400 m, a zigzag cliff stair about 120 m high, a cove with about 50 boats.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland on the island's east coast, 0.12 km up on red cliffs, a port at the cove below. Held by Lạc Hà Tông; named by the first mainland traders in 330. Nearest: beast lair Sài Quần Nguyên (90 km), ruin Vọng Phàm Quán (177 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Late afternoon: the grey roofs shine against the rust-red cliff, and a rust-coloured sail glows like an ember as a boat comes home.
places.subject: The place: Xích Ngạn Trấn, the Red Shore Town, a small walled town atop red sea cliffs. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle in late afternoon; a rugged forested headland of dark trees and red-brown rocky ridges drops in cliffs to the sea on every side but the south. The ridge crowns are dark with trees and the cliffs are streaked red-brown, ochre and rose where the rock shows. The town: a walled rectangle of grey stone on the plateau edge, with a gate tower and two corner towers, about fourteen hundred grey-tile roofs in tight rows, a main street leading to a central square, a pigment works at one side with ground-up red rock heaped in long red piles and shallow red-stained vats, drying yards with long bolts of sailcloth in rust-red hanging on frames, a harbour office, two inns, and a plain grey hall. Signature element: a very long stair cut into the cliff face, zigzagging back and forth a dozen times down the red rock from the town's cliff gate to the cove, with tiny people on it carrying baskets; at the foot about fifty boats drawn up on the beach and moored, nearly all of them under rust-red sails; the red water near the shore where pigment has washed down. Life at scale: a small, prosperous, colourful town and its working beach, hundreds of tiny figures. Light: warm gold afternoon light from the upper left raking the cliff, deep violet shadows in the cove, the red sails glowing.

places.name: Hải Yến Trấn
places.size: A fishing town of about 7,000 people: about 1,600 low grey roofs on a flat shore, each with deep double eaves, a small harbour of about 50 boats.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), flat grassland shore at sea level, a port. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: spirit vein Lục Âm Mạch (135 km), village Bối Sa Thôn (202 km), hot spring Ôn Bối Trì (247 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Dusk: the air above the eaves is a whirl of swallows going home to the nests, and a harvester on a ladder carries one nest in a basket.
places.subject: The place: Hải Yến Trấn, the Sea Swallow Town, a fishing town on a green island shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a rounded grassy cape of rolling green hills with a stream, a small rocky islet off its western shore and the open sea around it. The town: about sixteen hundred low grey roofs in long rows following the shore, each house wearing deep double eaves that overhang its walls by a full arm's length, so that from above every roof looks like a broad grey shield rimmed in white; under the eaves the nests of the sea swallows cluster so thickly that the eaves look whitewashed, a white fringe on every house. A broad main street runs from the harbour inland, with a nest-grading hall, a drying court with trays of cleaned nests on racks, an alchemists' buyers' inn, a net-loft and a fish market. A small harbour with a stone wall and about fifty low fishing boats. Signature element: the swallows, thousands of dark small birds in a vast whirling cloud above the town, pouring in and out of the eaves in the dusk, casting hundreds of tiny shadows on the roofs; here and there a harvester on a bamboo ladder, a speck, taking only an abandoned nest. Life at scale: a thickly settled, peaceful town with a tiny figure at every doorway. Light: soft rosy gold dusk light from the upper left, long shadows, the white fringes of the eaves bright.

places.name: Triều Âm Thành
places.size: A walled port city of about 30,000 people: about 7,000 grey roofs stepping up from the water, a stone breakwater about 800 m long bored with hundreds of round holes, a harbour of about 70 vessels.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland on the island's western shore at a river mouth, sea level, a port. Founded by Lạc Hà Tông in 540 as its western foothold. Nearest: beast lair Ngạc Bối Chử (79 km), village Phong Sào Thôn (257 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A rising tide at evening: the breakwater moans in a rising note, and the watchmen on the towers lean out to call the tide.
places.subject: The place: Triều Âm Thành, the Tide Song City, a walled harbour city on an island's western shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at evening, as the tide is flooding; a line of steep green grassy hills and a crest of ridges runs down the coast, dark forest in the south, white surf along a rocky shore, the sea on the left. The city: a walled shape of grey stone with towers, built on rising ground so the roofs step up from the water in terraces, about seven thousand grey-tile roofs in districts: a fisher quarter of low long roofs at the water, a merchants' quarter with warehouses and wide courts, a stone harbour with about seventy vessels, a grey-tile hall of the ruling sect on the highest terrace, a tide-watch tower, and rows of homes. Signature element: along the whole sea front runs a great stone breakwater, about eight hundred paces long and thick as a street, pierced along its length by hundreds of round holes, each a dark ring in the pale stone, through which the sea surges in white jets and spray as the tide comes in; a faint white haze lies along it; a few small boats of mainland musicians have anchored beside it, listening. Watchmen on the towers lean out. Life at scale: thousands of tiny figures on the quays and terraces. Light: low gold evening light from the upper left, the breakwater's spray glinting, long shadows toward the water.

places.name: Bối Sa Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 180 people: about 40 small houses on a gleaming white beach, a small mound-shrine of shells, drying mats, a handful of boats.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassy coast at 0.03 km, a white shell-sand beach, a port in a small way. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: hot spring Ôn Bối Trì (75 km), town Hải Yến Trấn (202 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A hot clear noon: families kneel along the tide line sifting shells, and a toddler is being lifted to set one shell on the white mound.
places.subject: The place: Bối Sa Thôn, the Shell Sands Village, a fishing village on a gleaming white beach. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at noon; a rounded grassy cape of green hills with a small islet off its south-western point, the sea on three sides. A broad crescent of dazzling white shell sand rims the cape, clear turquoise shallows fading to deep blue offshore, with beach grass behind. The village: about forty small houses with grey-tile and thatched roofs in two rough rows behind the shore line, each with a yard, a drying frame and a few upturned boats; a larger plain shed where shells are sorted, a well, a small wall of piled stone. Signature element: on the sand above the tide line stands a small rounded mound-shrine built entirely of white shells, bright as snow, about the height of a house, with a ring of worn stepping stones around it; around the shrine, on the sand, dozens of drying mats spread flat in neat patterns each heaped with sorted shells, white, pink, cream, striped; at the tide line rows of tiny figures bent over, gathering. About ten small fishing boats are drawn up on the beach, and two fishing in the shallows. Life at scale: a small, bright, humble community whose wealth lies on the sand. Fishers' wives wade the shallows with baskets, and a few small boats rock at anchor off the shell beach. Light: strong clean noon sun from the upper left, almost shadowless on the white sand, brilliant glints on the shell mounds and the water.

places.name: Lãng Thạch Thôn
places.size: A small fishing village of about 150 people: about 30 houses behind a sea stack about 60 m high, split in two, with a sea cave and a few boats.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassy coast at sea level, a port in a small way. Answers to Bình Thủy Môn. The sea stack split in a storm in 960 and opened a cave full of old charts. Nearest: beast lair Cự Ngao Chử (135 km), Bình Thủy Môn (158 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Low tide: a fisher rows a small party of visitors with lanterns through the gap into the dark mouth of the cave.
places.subject: The place: Lãng Thạch Thôn, the Wave Rock Village, a small fishing village behind a sea stack. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle in the morning; a blunt grassy headland of green hills, a small stream to the west, the sea running along its eastern side. A flat reef shows at low tide along the shore and white surf breaks over rocks beneath the headland's edge. The village: about thirty small grey-tile houses in a loose curve around a sheltered landing behind the stack, each with a yard, nets on poles and a few upturned boats; a larger shed where the island's visitors are met, a stone well, a path of white shells leading to the shore. Signature element: Wave Rock itself, a great sea stack about sixty paces tall, dark and wet, split from crown to waterline by a clean vertical gap wide enough for a boat, the two halves leaning slightly apart, with white foam at their feet; through the gap one can see the dark mouth of a sea cave, a black arch with calm green water running into it; a small rowing boat with a lantern at its prow is entering the gap with four tiny figures. On the flat rock at the cave's mouth, a few rolls of old waxed chart-paper lie drying in the sun. Life at scale: a quiet hamlet beside an enormous, ancient rock. Light: soft gold morning light from the upper left, deep shadow inside the gap, spray and foam glinting.

places.name: Dương Liễu Thôn
places.size: A dune-and-ridge village of about 170 people: about 35 grey-roofed houses sheltered by about 40 long rows of willows planted on the low ridges of a steep green coast, spread over about 400 m.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland coast at sea level, steep green hills and crags falling to the sea (the crop shows no flat dunes), a port in a small way. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: beast lair Phục Mãng Cương (90 km), spirit vein Tà Dương Mạch (325 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Windy late afternoon: the willows bend all one way in long green waves, and a woman buries a newborn's cord at the foot of a sapling.
places.subject: The place: Dương Liễu Thôn, the Willows Village, a village behind long rows of willows on a steep green coast. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle in late afternoon with a stiff sea wind; a steep rugged coast of green hills and bare grey crags falls to a deep blue sea along the left edge, white surf breaking on the rocks, small sandy pockets at the foot of the slopes. The village: about thirty-five small grey-tile houses with white-washed walls nestled in the hollows between the ridges, each household with its own yard and a vegetable plot; narrow earthen lanes wind between; a larger plain hall at the centre where the villagers meet, and a boat shed at a small landing in a cove. Signature element: about forty long rows of wind-bent willows planted along the crests of the low ridges, each row tended by one household, their long pale-green branches all streaming in one direction in the wind like green hair, their roots visibly binding the loose soil; from the sea the village looks hedged in a green maze. At the foot of one new sapling a tiny figure kneels with a small bundle; elsewhere a few villagers set stakes to guard new rows. Life at scale: small, gentle, entirely made by patient planting. Light: warm gold afternoon light from the upper left, shadows of the willow rows stretched long across the slopes. The willow rows are the only soft thing on this hard coast, each tended row a pale-green stripe against the grey-green slopes, and children carry water up from the stream to the youngest saplings in wooden buckets.

places.name: Tình Sa Thôn
places.size: A sandbar village of about 160 people: about 35 low grey houses on a sunny sandbar about 500 m long, with a driftwood whale effigy about 40 m long.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland at sea level on a sandbar at a river mouth, a port. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: hot spring Vũ Tễ Tuyền (75 km), ruin Bích Không Cảng (135 km), city Đàm Ảnh Thành (214 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: A sunny afternoon: villagers on ladders mending a rib of the driftwood whale with fresh silver planks while the river runs gold beside the bar.
places.subject: The place: Tình Sa Thôn, the Sunlit Sands Village, on a sunny sandbar at a river mouth. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright afternoon; green rolling hills and farmland, two streams meeting at the head of a narrow sea inlet that opens to the north, a river entering the inlet's mouth. Between the hills lies a pale sunny sandbar with channels of shining shallow water braiding through the sand where the river reaches the inlet. The village: about thirty-five low grey-roofed houses in two lines along the bar, each with a yard and a pole of drying fish, a small landing where about fifteen boats lie, a flat open square of sand where children play, a stone well. Signature element: on the bar beside the village lies a long driftwood effigy of a whale, about forty paces long, built of salvaged timbers, its ribs open like a ship's skeleton, its tail raised at one end and its great blunt head at the other, weathered to silver; it lies on its side as the real whale stranded, and a few small flags of pale cloth tie its ribs. Around it a scatter of new driftwood planks, and about ten tiny villagers mending it. Life at scale: a quiet, sunny hamlet around a monument to a kindness. A few terns hang over the shining channels, and the village's smoke rises straight in the still warm air. Light: warm bright afternoon sun from the upper left, long soft shadows of the ribs across the sand, glittering water.

places.name: Nguyệt Loan Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 250 people: about 45 houses around a perfect crescent cove about 500 m across, harbouring a crowded fleet of about 80 boats in a storm.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland coast at 0.04 km, a port; a crescent cove whose rock arms nearly close at the mouth. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: spirit vein Quế Ảnh Mạch (127 km); other places 389 km or more away. Water-qi.
places.imagined: The sky turns dark at the edge of a storm and boats are running for the cove from every side, their masts thick as reeds.
places.subject: The place: Nguyệt Loan Thôn, the Moon Cove Village, around a crescent bay. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle under a darkening sky at the edge of a storm; a steep rugged coast of green hills and ridges falls to the sea along the left edge, white surf breaking on every rock, and in one fold of the coast a small cove ringed by two arms of rock. The village: about forty-five small grey-tile houses in a curved row around the inner shore, each with a yard and a few upturned boats, a long timber boat shed with a carved wooden moon hung from its gable, a small stone harbour wall, a net-mending court, and a stone lookout on the northern arm with a small light. Signature element: the sheltered fleet, about eighty island boats of every kind packed in the cove, their masts thick as reeds, tied together side by side in rafts, with more boats running in through the narrow mouth under reefed sails; a few dozen tiny figures on the shore pulling lines; along the boat shed's gable many carved wooden moons in rows, thank-offerings from captains. Life at scale: a village swollen with a fleet, lamps being lit in the afternoon gloom. Light: dim, dramatic stormy light, a shaft of pale gold from the upper left through a break in the cloud falling on the cove, the surf white. On the cove's northern arm a small stone lookout holds a lamp that is kept burning in bad weather, and the captains' wooden moons turn slowly on their cords under the boat-shed eaves as the wind rises.

places.name: Bích Không Cảng
places.size: An emptied harbour, once a sailors' sect's port: long stone quays about 600 m out into the water, about 80 mooring posts, the roofless shell of a great sail loft about 80 m long; no boats, no people.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland coast at sea level, below Đàm Ảnh Thành. Cô Phàm Các's harbour, emptied when its fleet was lost; the widows left a year after. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: hot spring Vũ Tễ Tuyền (127 km), village Tình Sa Thôn (135 km), city Đàm Ảnh Thành (255 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A hazy blue morning: not one boat at the quays, and at the end of the longest quay a single tiny figure stands facing the open sea.
places.subject: The place: Bích Không Cảng, the Harbour of the Blue Sky, an empty harbour. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear, hazy, windless morning; a narrow sea inlet reaches into green rolling farmland hills, two rivers meeting at its head, hills rising on both sides and the open sea beyond. The harbour: three long stone quays run out in parallel from the shore into clear blue water, each about six hundred paces long and wide enough for carts, their stones pale and weathered, with grass growing in the cracks; along every quay a double row of bare wooden mooring posts, some eighty, grey and leaning, and not one boat anywhere; the water is perfectly empty and clear to a pale sandy bottom. At the root of the quays stands the roofless shell of a great sail loft, a hall about eighty paces long whose tile roof has gone, leaving only a stark ribbed frame of rafters open to the sky, with a few old sails rotted on the floor; around it, the foundations of about thirty warehouses and ropewalks, a stone slip, a plain cairn, an old lamp-post. Signature element: the emptiness, every post waiting; and one tiny figure, a woman in grey, sitting at the end of the longest quay. Life at scale: a place for a fleet that never came home, a huge quiet harbour that could hold two hundred ships. Light: soft pearl-gold light from the upper left, pale shadows, the blue haze.

places.name: Vụ Báo Lâm
places.size: A natural site: a steaming interior jungle about 30 km across drowned in mist, with a single black rock outcrop about 300 m long where the leopards bask. No buildings.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), jungle at 0.11 km, the island's interior; no coast shown. No sect holds it; ferrymen of Bình Thủy warn travellers off. Nearest: forest Nịch Tùng Lâm (160 km), villages Nam Minh Thôn (202 km) and Phương Lân Thôn (206 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Mid-morning: the mist is just burning through, and on the black outcrop three grey-spotted shapes lie flat as shadows.
places.subject: The place: Vụ Báo Lâm, the Mist Leopard Forest, a steaming jungle in the island's interior. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at mid-morning; dense dark jungle canopy cut by two winding rivers fills the frame, a rocky shore at the right edge and a foggy blue sea at the bottom. Thick white mist lies in the hollows and rises in slow wisps from the crowns, so the jungle is half drowned in fog; the canopy heaps like green cloud, dark glossy and tangled with vines, and thin veins of dark water show in the gaps. Out of the mist, near the centre, rises a single black rock outcrop about three hundred paces long with a flat sunlit top, where the mist is burning off round it. Signature element: on the flat top of the black rock, three or four grey-spotted leopards, seen as small pale shapes with darker rosettes, lying flat on the warm stone, nearly invisible against the grey-black; narrow bare paths wind through the undergrowth below the outcrop, and a few spots of bright orchid colour glow among the leaves. A few pale threads of vine hang over the rock's edge. No buildings, no camp, no roofline; at the very lower edge of the frame a single trail with the faint mark of an old ferryman's cairn. Life at scale: an enormous, hot, quiet wildness. Light: warm gold morning light from the upper left piercing the mist in soft shafts, deep green shadows, steam glowing.

places.name: Cự Ngao Chử
places.size: The crab flats and a young seat: about 60 sect members (ferrymen, sailors, shipwrights) in a new settlement of about 45 buildings, mostly timber on stilts at the edge of a vast tidal flat about 5 km across, where giant crabs roam. Not yet old; a rough, new-built home.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), grassland at sea level (0.0 km), a low tidal shoal on the coast, beast lair of giant crabs. The sect Bình Thủy Môn moved its seat here in 1116 (from place 18). Nearest: village Lãng Thạch Thôn (135 km), Bình Thủy Môn (266 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Low tide at noon: the flats stretch out wet and silver, a few huge crab claws rise from the mud like pale trees, and the ferrymen's stilt houses stand above.
places.subject: The place: Cự Ngao Chử, the Shoal of the Great Claws, a grassy headland with a tidal flat that is now a ferrymen's sect seat. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at low tide at noon; a rounded green grassy headland with a few dark conifer groves and a small stream system runs out into the sea, turquoise shallows along its eastern shore. A strip of pale shell sand and shallow pools edges the shore beyond the tidal flat. The settlement: about forty-five buildings on timber stilts and low earth platforms along the shore, with grey-tile and thatched roofs, newly built and still raw, joined by long board walks out over the mud: a main hall with a double roof, two long dormitories, a shipwright's yard with three hulls on stocks and a dry dock cut into the mud, a boat-landing with about twenty ferries and fishing craft lying on the flat at low tide, net-lofts, a smithy, and a few dozen homes. Signature element: the crabs, a scatter of about a dozen huge crabs, each the size of a house, pale red-grey with enormous claws raised, scattered across the flats like boulders, with tiny ferrymen leading a line of laden boats on skids around them; one claw pokes from a pit near the walkway. Life at scale: a rough, vigorous young settlement on the edge of a wild shore. Small flocks of grey shorebirds work the shallow pools along the edge of the flat. Light: bright noon sun from the upper left, silver glare on the wet mud, short crisp shadows.

places.name: Nhàn Vân Quán
places.size: A tiny painters' sect of about 30 painters and servants: about 25 buildings in a small walled garden compound about 150 m across, wide open studios under pale roofs; a modest, airy place.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), steppe at 0.04 km on the coast of the island, vassal of Lạc Hà Tông, neutral. The sect keeps a Pool House in the city Đàm Ảnh Thành. Nearest places are 326 km or more away (beast lair Hào Trư Lĩnh), so it stands alone. Water-qi.
places.imagined: A late afternoon with high clouds: painters sit at open pavilions' edges with easels turned to the sky, and clouds drift over the pale roofs.
places.subject: The place: Nhàn Vân Quán, the Abbey of the Idle Clouds, a small painters' retreat on the dry grass of an island coast. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright late afternoon with great slow white clouds; a green grassy coast with pockets of rust-orange scrub and a few dark conifer groves runs diagonally under the sea at the top right. The abbey: about twenty-five buildings inside a low whitewashed wall around a central garden: a long main studio hall with its whole south side open and a broad pale-grey tile roof sweeping low, three smaller open-sided studios, a gallery for drying canvases with long racks, a grinding house for pigments, a kitchen court, and sleeping cells for thirty, all of pale wood and pale roofs, airy and wide; a shallow garden pool in the centre reflects the sky, with stepping stones and a small plank bridge. Signature element: the many large canvases and silk screens set out on frames in the garden and on the open terraces, turned to face the sky, hung with pale and blue paintings of clouds, a dozen or more, so the whole compound looks as if it were made to hold the sky; about twenty tiny painters in pale smocks at easels, one lying on his back in the grass. Life at scale: a quiet, small community given over entirely to watching. Light: soft warm gold afternoon light from the upper left, the clouds' shadows drifting across the grass, gentle shadows under the eaves.

places.name: Phiêu Bồng Quán
places.size: A ruined abbey of a vanished small sect: about 20 buildings once, in a compound about 200 m across on open steppe, now roofless and drifted with dry brush; a hermit's hut in one corner.
places.where: Region 10 (Cô Vụ Đảo), steppe at 0.06 km on the coast, a former sect, held by Lạc Hà Tông. The depth pages: tenants now are beasts, or a hermit who claims the master's books were never hers to give. Nearest: market Tương Phùng Thị (103 km), spirit vein Bình Tung Mạch (125 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A windy afternoon: tumbleweeds roll through the open gate and fetch up against the broken walls, and the hermit's chimney sends one thin thread of smoke.
places.subject: The place: Phiêu Bồng Quán, the Abbey of the Drifting Tumbleweed, a ruin on dry steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a dry windy afternoon; a narrow green grassy peninsula tipped with a tongue of rust-orange scrub and dark trees runs north, the turquoise sea on three sides. The ruin: about twenty buildings arranged round a square courtyard and a double gate, all of grey stone and once grey-tile, now with roofs collapsed, walls cracked and half down, door frames empty, floors drifted with sand and dry brush; the main hall has lost its entire roof, leaving a ribbed row of rafters like a fishbone; broken pillars lie in the courtyard, and a dry well stands at its centre. A line of old stone steps leads nowhere. Signature element: the tumbleweeds, a drift of about a hundred of them, piled against the abbey's windward wall and caught in the open gate and doors, so the old halls look stuffed with dry brush; in one corner a small repaired hut with a re-thatched roof and a single thread of smoke, the hermit's, and in front of it a few shelves of old books under a small awning, and a tiny grey-cloaked figure looking out at the sea. A pair of beasts, small tawny steppe cats, lie on a broken wall. Life at scale: a bare place of drifting things. Light: low dry gold afternoon light from the upper left, long shadows of the wall-ends across the sand, haze of dust.

places.name: Mục Vân Trang
places.size: A minor sect of about 80 people and 2,000 spirit horses: a manor of about 60 buildings on a low rise about 350 m across, wrapped by a great oval track about 3 km round, with paddocks and stables across several square kilometres.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên, the open plain), grassland on the coast at 0.04 km, a low rise near the sea. Founded 740 by herders; sworn to Lạc Hà Tông, neutral. Nearest: spirit vein Trì Vân Mạch (75 km), ruin Di Hà Trấn (158 km), town Thanh Điền Trấn (177 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A race morning: pale spirit horses run the oval like a drifting cloud, riders low on their necks, and the stable tower stands over them.
places.subject: The place: Mục Vân Trang, the Cloud-Herding Manor, a spirit-horse sect on a grassy coast of the open plain. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright morning with a clear wide sky; green and gold grassland rolls away inland behind lobed headlands and fingers of land with dark groves that reach out into the sea. The manor: about sixty buildings on a low rise, grey-tile roofs over pale timber walls climbing in tiers to a tall stable tower under a sweeping grey roof, the tallest outline on the plain; below it four very long stable halls, each about a hundred paces, a riders' barracks, a training yard with posts and jumps, a farrier and saddlery court, hay barns with huge stacks, a feed mill, a main hall and about twenty small houses of the grooms. Signature element: round the whole foot of the rise runs a great oval racing track of packed pale earth, about three kilometres round, wide as a main road, and on it about forty pale spirit horses, white and cream with faint glowing manes, run in a long streaming line, so that they move like a cloud; dust drifting behind them. Beyond the track, fenced paddocks scattered with hundreds of grazing horses, and herds of a thousand more on the plain, tiny pale dots; a few riders in grey. Life at scale: a ranch the size of a small town in its own country. Light: golden morning light from the upper left, long shadows of the horses, dust glowing.

places.name: Nhạn Thanh Thành
places.size: A walled port city of about 40,000 people, the wool market of the western plain: walls about 2.5 km on a side, some 9,000 roofs, big wool warehouses, a harbour at a river mouth with about 60 vessels.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), steppe at sea level on the coast where a river meets the sea, a port. Founded 450 by Lạc Hà Tông. Nearest: lake Lạc Nhạn Hồ (168 km), village Vãn Chu Thôn (283 km), the minor sect Nhạn Trận Môn (301 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Autumn: a long V of wild geese passes low over the gate tower, whose two upswept roofs spread like wings, and no archer lifts a bow.
places.subject: The place: Nhạn Thanh Thành, the City of the Wild Geese's Cry, a walled wool-trading city on the dry steppe coast. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear autumn afternoon; a bay cuts into rolling tawny-green hills with dark forest pockets and a rocky coast, a long thin lake lies in the hills behind and a river runs to the shore. The city: grey stone walls about two and a half kilometres on a side with square towers, a land gate and a river gate; inside, about nine thousand grey-tile roofs crowded around wool warehouses: great long barn-like halls, thirty of them, with piles of grey and cream fleece bales in the yards; wool-washing basins along the river, dyers' yards with vats of colours and cloth hung in long coloured bands, a vast open market square for the wool auctions, the grand house of the richest merchant, a grey-tile hall of the ruling sect, and dense lanes of houses. A harbour with about sixty vessels, flat wool barges and small ships. Signature element: over the main gate rises a tower whose two upswept grey roofs spread like the wings of a goose in flight; over the city a long V of about forty wild geese passes low, casting small shadows on the roofs; no archer on the walls. Life at scale: carts of wool bales in long lines on the roads, tens of thousands of tiny figures. Light: warm amber autumn light from the upper left, long shadows, colours of the dyers' cloth glowing.

places.name: Thanh Điền Trấn
places.size: A small walled market town of about 5,000 people: about 1,100 roofs inside a wall about 600 m across, in a sea of fields several kilometres wide, with hundreds of horses at hitching rails.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland at the coast at sea level, a port, in endless farmland. Held by Mục Vân Trang, whose head was born here in 940. Nearest: ruin Di Hà Trấn (79 km), spirit veins Trì Vân Mạch and Ẩn Canh Mạch (135 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: A horse-fair morning: farmers ride in from every direction along the field tracks and tie up along the hitching rails outside the gate.
places.subject: The place: Thanh Điền Trấn, the Green Fields Town, a market town in a sea of fields. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright spring morning; a lobed grassy coast of gold-green hills and dark groves with the sea to the north and pockets of farm plots in the south. Long hedgerows and irrigation ditches divide the farm plots, and straight dirt tracks run between them. The town: a small walled rectangle of grey stone about six hundred paces across, one gate on each side, about eleven hundred grey-tile roofs in orderly streets around a market square with a grain exchange, a few big granaries, a harness-maker's street, and a small grey hall answering to the horse sect. Signature element: outside the main gate stretches a very long row of hitching rails, a hundred and fifty paces long, with hundreds of horses tied along it, brown, bay and a few pale, since the fields are too far to walk; more riders arrive along the field tracks as tiny dots, and children on ponies race along the ditch banks; a small horse-fair ring of rope on the green beside the gate. Life at scale: a small town surrounded by thousands of tiny farmers on horseback working the far plots. Dust rises behind riders on the tracks, and in the fields small herds of cattle graze under the hedges. Light: bright clean morning light from the upper left, the fields glowing in different greens, soft long shadows of the hedgerows.

places.name: Thảo Đường Thành
places.size: A farm-and-pond city of about 25,000 people: walls about 1.8 km along a side, some 6,000 low grey roofs, and a chequerboard of about 800 square ponds around it across about 10 km.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland on the flat coastal plain at sea level, a port. Founded 680 by Lạc Hà Tông among farms. Nearest: ruin Dã Độ Trấn (90 km), villages Lô Cảng Thôn (158 km) and Yến Quy Thôn (160 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A calm afternoon: hundreds of square ponds, each a bright square of sky, with ducks making white wakes and families on the grass banks.
places.subject: The place: Thảo Đường Thành, the Grass Pond City, a walled farming city among gold-green coastal hills. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a calm bright afternoon; a lobed coast of gold-green hills and dark groves with the sea to the north and small farm plots and a stream in the south. Between the hills lie small farm plots, ditches and a stream where the ponds are dug. The city: a square wall of grey stone about eighteen hundred paces on a side with four gates, enclosing about six thousand low grey-tile roofs that sit low among farms, with orchard gardens and drying yards inside the wall; a modest market square, a grain hall, a hemp-rope walk with long ropes laid out in lines, a duck-and-fish market, a grey hall of the ruling sect. Signature element: outside the walls lies a vast chequerboard of about eight hundred grass-banked square ponds, each a square of reflected sky, blue or pale gold, edged with green grass banks wide enough to walk; each family owns one square and the banks are common; fish nets, duck-pens, small boats of reeds, ducks making tiny white wakes, white flocks of ducks on the banks, with rice paddies and hemp fields interspersed. Tiny families picnic on the banks; a slow market-day crowd walks in along the grass banks toward the gate. Life at scale: a calm, friendly, prosperous farm town whose land is half water. Light: soft warm afternoon light from the upper left, every pond reflecting the sky, long gentle shadows.
